props.characteristic: who or what produced the quantity the procedure is driven toward
props.positive_test: the procedure is fitted to something; name what supplies it
props.negative_test: the procedure fits nothing
props.examples: all values below
props.notes: multi-valued

props.characteristic: what kind of agent produced the annotation
props.positive_test: the target was produced by an agent outside the run's own model and environment
props.negative_test: the target is computed from the input itself
props.examples: labels, preferences, demonstrations

props.positive_test: a person assigned the target value to the example
props.negative_test: a model or a rule assigned it
props.examples: ImageNet labels, annotated spans, human ratings

props.positive_test: another trained model produced the target the learner is fitted to
props.negative_test: the learner produced its own target
props.examples: knowledge distillation teacher logits, synthetic instruction data, RLAIF labels, pseudo-labels from a different model
props.notes: distinct from self-labelling, which is S.src.self.own

props.positive_test: a rule, heuristic, lexicon or metadata field supplied the target
props.negative_test: a human adjudicated each example
props.examples: Snorkel labelling functions, distant supervision, regex labels, metadata-derived labels

props.positive_test: the target is a relative judgement between two or more candidates, not an absolute value
props.negative_test: the target is an absolute score or class
props.examples: RLHF comparison pairs, learning-to-rank relevance judgements, KTO thumbs

props.positive_test: the target is an action sequence produced by an expert acting in the task
props.negative_test: the target is a scalar score of the agent's own behaviour
props.examples: behaviour-cloning trajectories, DAgger corrections, teleoperated robot data

props.positive_test: supervision comes from items that were observed together in the world, not annotated
props.negative_test: an annotator created the association
props.examples: image-alt-text pairs for CLIP, audio-video sync, translation bitext, click logs
props.notes: boundary between supervised and self-supervised

props.positive_test: the target is a quantity recorded as an attribute of the unit -- an outcome, a response, a measurement -- including a categorical response, with no annotator deciding it for the purpose of supervision
props.negative_test: a value an annotator assigned to an example in order to supervise a model (S.src.ext.human); a value a rule computed (S.src.ext.prog)
props.examples: the response in a regression, the outcome in a trial, a survival time, a measured covariate
props.notes: added after pinning: 169 nodes across the classical branch were parked on the interior node S.src.ext for want of this, so every S.src.ext.* roll-up read `unknown annotation type` when the truth is `no annotator exists`. Tests sharpened during the migration: the first wording did not separate a respondent from an annotator, and ~40 tree/ensemble/GLM nodes turn entirely on that -- a diagnosis or a survey answer is person-assigned but is not an annotation

props.positive_test: the target is feedback returned after the system acted
props.negative_test: the target exists before the system acts
props.examples: game score, verifier pass/fail, curiosity bonus

props.positive_test: an external environment or simulator emits the scalar being maximised
props.negative_test: the scalar is computed by a model the run also trained
props.examples: Atari score, MuJoCo reward, game win/loss

props.positive_test: a deterministic checker decides correctness of the produced output
props.negative_test: a learned model judges the output
props.examples: unit-test pass, exact-match answer check, compiler success, formal proof check
props.notes: the RLVR branch

props.positive_test: the reward is emitted by a model fitted on external judgements
props.negative_test: the reward comes from the environment directly
props.examples: RLHF reward models, process reward models, LLM-as-judge reward
props.notes: derived from preferences, hence multi-parent

props.positive_test: the reward is computed from the agent's own prediction error, novelty or counts
props.negative_test: the reward is supplied from outside the agent
props.examples: RND bonus, ICM error, pseudo-counts, empowerment, DIAYN diversity reward

props.characteristic: which part of the input plays the role of target
props.positive_test: the target is a deterministic function of the unlabelled input
props.negative_test: a separate agent or environment supplied the target
props.examples: masked tokens, augmented views, noise added by the method

props.positive_test: part of the input is removed and the procedure predicts exactly what was removed
props.negative_test: the input is perturbed but nothing is withheld for prediction
props.examples: BERT masked tokens, MAE masked patches, span corruption, inpainting

props.positive_test: the target is the continuation of an observed prefix, in time or sequence order
props.negative_test: the target is a hidden element of a bidirectional context
props.examples: next-token prediction, PixelCNN, future-frame prediction, CPC futures

S.src.self.view.name: A second view of the same instance

props.positive_test: two transformed copies of one instance are made and compared to each other
props.negative_test: one copy only, compared to a stored label
props.examples: SimCLR views, BYOL views, SwAV views, multi-crop

props.positive_test: noise of known magnitude is added and the procedure must undo or score it
props.negative_test: a transformation whose inverse is not the learning target
props.examples: DDPM noise, denoising autoencoder noise, score matching perturbation

props.positive_test: the target is the whole input, reproduced with no part hidden and no noise added
props.negative_test: part of the input is withheld or corrupted first
props.examples: autoencoder reconstruction, VAE reconstruction term, PCA reconstruction, self-reconstruction losses
props.notes: added after the VAE worked example found no fitting value

props.positive_test: the learner's own current, averaged or past prediction serves as the target
props.negative_test: another model produced the target
props.examples: pseudo-labelling, Mean Teacher EMA targets, self-training, self-consistency, bootstrapped values
props.notes: includes RL bootstrapping

props.positive_test: the objective is defined on the geometry or statistics of the whole dataset, not per example
props.negative_test: a per-example target
props.examples: k-means distortion, PCA variance, t-SNE neighbourhoods, topic-model likelihood
props.notes: the classical-unsupervised home

props.characteristic: what feature of the design creates the counterfactual contrast
props.positive_test: the target is a contrast between conditions that a design argues is comparable
props.negative_test: the target is a predictive association with no comparability claim
props.examples: RCT arms, propensity-matched pairs, instrument, discontinuity

props.positive_test: treatment was assigned at random by the experimenter
props.negative_test: treatment was observed as it occurred
props.examples: A/B tests, randomised controlled trials, randomised encouragement

props.positive_test: comparability is claimed after conditioning on measured covariates
props.negative_test: comparability comes from an instrument, threshold or time structure
props.examples: propensity matching, IPW, AIPW, double ML, g-computation

props.positive_test: comparability comes from an instrument, a threshold or a pre/post panel
props.negative_test: comparability comes from covariate adjustment alone
props.examples: 2SLS instruments, regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences, synthetic control

props.positive_test: the signal is the pattern of statistical (in)dependences used to orient edges
props.negative_test: the signal is an effect magnitude
props.examples: PC algorithm tests, FCI, GES score differences, LiNGAM non-Gaussianity

props.characteristic: what kind of prior knowledge is imposed
props.positive_test: the target is the residual of an equation or constraint assumed true a priori
props.negative_test: a target measured from data
props.examples: PDE residuals, conservation laws, logical constraints

props.positive_test: the loss contains the residual of a differential equation evaluated at sampled points
props.negative_test: the equation is used only to generate training data
props.examples: PINN residual loss, Deep Ritz, Hamiltonian NN constraint

props.positive_test: the loss penalises violation of a declared logical or algebraic constraint
props.negative_test: the constraint is enforced by construction in the architecture
props.examples: semantic loss, constraint-satisfaction penalties, Lagrangian constraint terms
props.notes: speculative outside neuro-symbolic venues

S.src.meas.name: A measured score from the run itself

props.positive_test: the target is a performance figure the procedure obtained by running or simulating a candidate -- a validation score, a held-out metric, a win rate, a fitness
props.negative_test: a reward emitted by an environment the agent acted in (S.src.env.reward); a target attached to an example (S.src.ext.*)
props.examples: AutoAugment's validation accuracy, NAS-RL's accuracy reward, Bayesian-optimisation observations, Hyperband budgets, MAP-Elites fitness
props.notes: added in D.1: four of six pinning regions proposed this gap independently under four different names (S.form.sel.metric, S.src.meas, S.src.env.metric, S.src.trial), which is the strongest convergence signal this process produced. It sits under S.src rather than S.src.ext because the quantity is produced by the run, not supplied to it

props.positive_test: the procedure has no quantity it is fitted to; it transforms or selects instead
props.negative_test: any fitted parameter, even a single calibration statistic
props.examples: beam search, top-p sampling, BPE merges (counting, not fitting), CutMix, gradient clipping, FSDP sharding
props.notes: essential: roughly a third of the dimension sits here

props.characteristic: how the gap between model output and target is turned into a number
props.positive_test: name the functional form of the training criterion
props.negative_test: the procedure has no criterion
props.examples: all values below
props.notes: multi-valued

props.positive_test: maximises a normalised log-probability the model can compute exactly
props.negative_test: maximises a bound or an unnormalised score
props.examples: cross-entropy, autoregressive LM loss, GLM likelihood, normalizing-flow likelihood, MLE

props.positive_test: maximises a tractable lower bound on an intractable log-likelihood
props.negative_test: maximises the exact likelihood
props.examples: ELBO, IWAE bound, variational EM, SVI, beta-VAE objective

props.positive_test: regresses the gradient of the log-density, or equivalently the added noise
props.negative_test: regresses the clean data point itself
props.examples: score matching, denoising score matching, DDPM epsilon-prediction, flow-matching velocity

props.positive_test: penalises a distance between a reconstruction and the original input
props.negative_test: penalises a distance between two different instances' representations
props.examples: autoencoder MSE, MAE pixel loss, PCA reconstruction, VQ codebook loss

props.positive_test: the loss has explicit negatives whose similarity is pushed down
props.negative_test: the loss only pulls positives together
props.examples: InfoNCE, NT-Xent, triplet loss, BPR pairwise loss, noise-contrastive estimation

props.positive_test: regresses one branch onto a target branch, with no negatives and a stop-gradient or EMA
props.negative_test: uses negatives, or a fixed external label
props.examples: BYOL, SimSiam, Mean Teacher consistency, SPR latent loss, data2vec
props.notes: collapse-avoidance is the signature

props.positive_test: drives an embedding cross-correlation or covariance matrix toward a target structure
props.negative_test: compares individual sample pairs
props.examples: Barlow Twins, VICReg, W-MSE, whitening losses

props.positive_test: penalises violations of a required separation between scores
props.negative_test: penalises probability error
props.examples: hinge loss, SVM margin, triplet margin, large-margin softmax

props.positive_test: minimises total distance of points to assigned representatives or a layout
props.negative_test: minimises a probabilistic loss
props.examples: k-means distortion, MDS stress, t-SNE KL over neighbour distributions, OT cost

props.positive_test: the criterion is a minimax between two optimisers with opposed objectives
props.negative_test: both terms are minimised by the same optimiser
props.examples: GAN objective, WGAN critic, DANN domain adversary, adversarial training inner max, GAIL

props.positive_test: maximises a discounted sum of future scalars, with credit assigned across time
props.negative_test: maximises a per-example score with no temporal credit
props.examples: policy gradient surrogates, Bellman TD error, PPO clipped surrogate, Q-learning loss

props.positive_test: minimises an explicit divergence or moment discrepancy between two distributions
props.negative_test: minimises a per-example loss
props.examples: MMD, CORAL, KL to a teacher, Sinkhorn divergence, moment matching
props.notes: distillation's form when it is not plain cross-entropy

props.positive_test: chooses parameters by setting a sample moment or influence-function equation to zero
props.negative_test: minimising a loss by descent
props.examples: method of moments, GMM-IV, Z-estimation, TMLE targeting step, estimating equations in GEE
props.notes: added after the TMLE worked example found no fitting value

props.positive_test: the loss depends only on the order of scores, not their absolute values
props.negative_test: the loss depends on absolute score values
props.examples: DPO loss, Bradley-Terry likelihood, LambdaRank, ListNet, pairwise ranking loss
props.notes: Bradley-Terry is also a likelihood; both values apply

props.positive_test: penalises violation of an equation or constraint evaluated on sampled points
props.negative_test: penalises distance to observed data
props.examples: PINN PDE residual, Lagrangian penalty, semantic loss

props.positive_test: the procedure's criterion is correctness of a posterior, whether approached by sampling or obtained in closed form
props.negative_test: the criterion is a point estimate's loss
props.examples: MCMC detailed balance, SMC weighting, Bayes rule updates
props.notes: no gradient descent needed to satisfy it; test widened after pinning: it said `approached by sampling`, which excluded the closed-form posteriors of Gaussian processes, Kalman filters, Laplace approximation and expectation propagation -- about 25 of its own 53 pins contradicted it

props.positive_test: the criterion is a function of the model's own output confidence only
props.negative_test: the criterion involves any target outside the model's output
props.examples: entropy minimisation (TENT), confidence penalty, FixMatch thresholding, pseudo-label confidence gating

props.positive_test: penalises the number or magnitude of active components, independent of fit
props.negative_test: penalises fit error
props.examples: L1 penalty, nuclear norm, MDL, AIC/BIC selection, sparse-autoencoder L1
props.notes: usually appears alongside a fit term

props.positive_test: penalises variation of the output under a declared nuisance transformation or environment
props.negative_test: penalises error on the observed distribution only
props.examples: IRM penalty, consistency regularisation, GroupDRO worst-group risk, VAT

props.positive_test: targets a stated frequency guarantee on a held-out distribution
props.negative_test: targets average accuracy
props.examples: conformal quantile calibration, conformal risk control, quantile pinball loss

S.form.metric.name: Comparison of candidates by a measured score

props.positive_test: candidates are ranked or selected by a measured figure of merit, with no loss differentiated and no parameters updated by it
props.negative_test: a differentiable validation loss (that is an ordinary criterion); a reward maximised by a policy-gradient estimator (S.form.return)
props.examples: hyperparameter search, evolutionary and reinforcement-learning architecture search, population-based training, augmentation-policy search
props.notes: added in D.1 with S.src.meas. Every other S.form value is a criterion an optimiser minimises; selecting configurations by a held-out number is not, which is why all of L.hpo, L.nas and L.automl resolved to nothing

props.positive_test: compares replicate, permuted or held-out values of a statistic in order to quantify its error, coverage or significance, fitting no parameters in the process
props.negative_test: a criterion that parameters are fitted to; selecting among candidates by a measured score (S.form.metric)
props.examples: the bootstrap, jackknife, permutation tests, k-fold cross-validation as an error estimate, Neyman-Pearson tests, FDR control
props.notes: added 2026-10-07, closing the last non-data-dependent item on #96. The owner ruled assessment procedures in scope, which left L.boot and L.test (27 nodes) resolving to no signal: S.form.none is false for a bootstrap interval, because it genuinely does compare something. It is distinct from S.form.metric -- that one selects a candidate, this one quantifies an error

props.positive_test: the procedure performs no comparison between an output and a target
props.negative_test: any fitted or calibrated quantity
props.examples: beam search, all-reduce, pipeline scheduling, magnitude pruning, BPE
